notes: No coherent unique-token-to-fixed-target circuit was identified. This is a moderate-confidence negative weight-only assessment, not a proof of absence. Embedding norms are heavy-tailed (median 0.3793, p99 1.9501, max 3.3871 at token 523), but multiple tokens are outliers and their centered directions have close neighbors: 523/614 cosine 0.9852, 167/662 cosine 0.9875. Raw direct-route leader token 167 points to class 5, whereas raw linearized MLP leader token 98 points to class 3; magnitude-normalized products show no isolated leader. MLP neuron read directions have maximum top-two token alignment gap 0.03132. Attention W_o is nearly rank one (97.34% top singular-value energy); per-head OV concentration is 97.95% and 99.83%, but OV norms are only 0.02296 and 0.11648. Centered unit-direction OV leaders are shared across tokens and classes 7/4, without a corresponding unique QK selector. Conservative global per-head attention-score-spread bounds are 0.4984 and 2.4394, implying single-position attention upper bounds 0.3543 and 0.7926 for four positions. These bounds exclude arbitrarily sharp attention, not moderate-attention backdoors. Variable per-head OV residual-output norm bounds are 0.0552 and 0.3399. Classifier and MLP spectra do not show a single dominating class writer. Comparisons use within-checkpoint token ranks, spectral energies, and algebraic bounds; there is no clean reference, empirical null calibration, or behavioral validation. Virtual paths include LN centering and learned scales, but omit input-dependent normalization denominators and nonlinear GELU gating; they are not logits or predictions. Ordinary token-to-class lookup can itself produce fixed-class last-token associations, so that alone is not evidence of a backdoor. No sequence inputs, forward passes, training, or weight modifications were used.

evidence.calibration: Within-checkpoint descriptive statistics and analytic bounds only; no reference-model or behavioral calibration.
